reuse.why: All month-wide fills, including the new last-month action, go through one isCategoryFilled predicate and one averageToBudgetAmount, and keep using getBudgetData, getCategoryAverage and setNMonthAvg.

duplication.why: setZero repeats the categories/groups/notes SELECT that getAverageFillCategories already wraps, and the 'zero' and 'copy' switch arms are identical.

placement.why: Selection rules live together in budget/actions.ts next to the actions that use them; the template and #fixed checks could arguably sit with the template/notes code but nothing there already provides them.

scope.why: Mostly focused, but resetIncomeCarryover gains an includeHiddenCategories parameter it never uses, and averageToBudgetAmount is reused for non-average last-month spending under a misleading name.

maintainability.why: One predicate owns the rule, but the kind switch adds an average-only hidden/group check that re-states the hidden rule a second time in a ternary, and the duplicated query must be kept in sync.

abstraction_drift.where: isCategoryFilled (budget/actions.ts) gains includeHiddenCategories and its 'average' arm re-tests hidden/group_hidden through an includeHiddenCategories ternary; resetIncomeCarryover gets the flag without using the predicate
